items.title: 67247_J.C. Higginbotham oral history interview
items.q: But they caught up with Louis Russell and put a fine on him. Otis Johnson, trumpet player, said, "I'm not going to give back nothing. I played for that and I'm keeping it."

ctx.x: So in other words the club owner was reporting that you were making the scale but the fact was -

They would pay you the scale and you'd give the scale to the union. The union would give you your money and you'd take that $25 or $30 and give it back to the man that owned the place. But they caught up with Louis Russell and put a fine on him. Otis Johnson, trumpet player, said, "I'm not going to give back nothing. I played for that and I'm keeping it." So we had a trial board and they didn't fine Russell or nothing like that. They just called him the black sheep of the family... He apologized in a hurry too.…
Yeah, the kickback, right. Was that even the practice at the Apollo and the Savoy?
